precision.bottom: Rows the model gave this category

recall.bottom: Rows that really are this category

specificity.top: Rows correctly kept out of this category
specificity.bottom: Rows that really are not this category

metricHelp.accuracy: The share of all rows the model got right. It reads easily, but it misleads when the classes are imbalanced — if 90 of 100 rows share one category, answering with that category every time already scores 90%. Read it together with the other scores.
metricHelp.f1: A score that reflects precision and recall together, so a high score on only one of them does not lift it — 90% precision with 10% recall gives an F1 of 18%. It is worked out for each category, and this model’s F1 score is the average of those.
metricHelp.precision: Of the rows the model answered with this category, the share that really were this category. What matters is the denominator: the model’s own answers. In a factory test, it asks how many of the parts pulled aside as faulty really were faulty. A low number means the model reaches for this category too often and throws out good parts with the bad.
metricHelp.recall: Of the rows that really are this category, the share the model found. The denominator is the truth, and that is what separates it from precision — in the same factory test, it asks how many of the truly faulty parts were caught, because the ones missed ship out. Missing a category and over-using it are different problems, so read the two together.
metricHelp.specificity: Of the rows that are not this category, the share the model correctly kept out of it. In a medical test it is the ability to tell a healthy person they are healthy; when it is low, rows get labelled with this category by mistake and false alarms pile up. It is easy to confuse with precision: both punish the same mistake, but precision divides by the model’s answers while specificity divides by every row that truly is not this category.
metricHelp.support: How many rows of the evaluation data really are this category. It counts the data used for scoring, not the data used for training. When it is small, the scores beside it swing on a single row — in a category of three rows, getting one more right lifts recall by 33 points.
metricHelp.r2: How much of the variation in the values the model explains. Closer to 1 is better, and it goes negative when the model does worse than always guessing the average.
metricHelp.rmse: How far the predictions land from the real values on average. Large misses count for more, and the unit is the same as the value being predicted.
metricHelp.mae: How far the predictions land from the real values on average. Every miss counts the same, so it stays steadier when a few values are extreme.
